# Fourier request host integration

Status: composite checker, theorem and fresh native/host path implemented on
2026-09-29. Production hierarchy/source acceptance remains separate.

The actual complete-entry Fourier inspector is now proved. Connect it to the
existing strict hierarchy request API, starting from the existing shared QFT
producer and independent singleton `qft` requests at widths 1–8. Preserve the
earlier desired sized `.qli` source and finite/gradient counterexamples.

Compose complete artifact checking and Fourier inspection in one pure Lean
entry point, with the unchanged aggregate structural budget. Prove the same
actual value has the requested Fourier matrix, unitary interface and reference
inverse laws under both returned sets of finite obligations.

The external JSON request remains `qleisli.hierarchy-request` version 1. Its
singleton Fourier form has equation/unitary kind/effect, entry zero and one
`qft` meaning with the same complete interface and width. Carry that whole
independent request through a separate bounded private frame; validate its
shape again before invoking the pure composite checker. Rust proposes only the
wiring dependency schedule. Every finite proof and actual H index returned by a
fresh native process must be reconstructed from the same immutable artifact;
compare H against its independent exact, phase-fixed matrix using the remaining
exact budget. No native response or producer flag is a caller-supplied receipt.

Retain the existing API and raw input bytes. This additive checked request report
does not become a production `VerifiedProgram`, enable external schema IDs or
discharge native/decoder correspondence. Validate coordinated circuit/meaning
faults against unchanged requests, stale finite bytes, wrong request fields,
truncated/cross-mode responses, omitted/duplicated H obligations, full typing,
aggregate work and shared finite-reader budgets. Keep existing request behavior
and capacity regressions. Preserve first sources and actual failures.

The [native record](fourier-host-native.json) passes 187 binary cases and 39
host scenarios, including the closed `Bits<n>` boundary counterexamples.
Width eight uses 1,933,823 structural and 944 exact units. The
[registry audit](fourier-host-registry.json), [Rust checks](fourier-host-rust-validation.json)
and [runtime regressions](fourier-host-runtime-validation.json) retain validation;
[first attempts](fourier-host-first/README.md) preserve actual failures.
